source_text: baptisma, inquiunt, omnibus necessarium esse aetatibus confitemur, gratiam quoque adiuvare uniuscuiusque bonum propositum, non tamen reluctanti studium virtutis immittere, quia personarum acceptio non est apud Deum
pass_a_gloss: We confess baptism to be necessary for all ages, and grace also to help each one's good purpose, yet not to send in the pursuit of virtue to one who resists, because there is no acceptance of persons with God.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: We confess that baptism is necessary at every age, and that grace also helps each person’s good purpose, but does not plant the pursuit of virtue in someone who resists, because there is no partiality with God (Colossians 3:25; Romans 2:11).

choices.why: In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.
Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian and fellow bishops (Collective letter to Thessalonica, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 2–4); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
